proposed.text: An architect is revising a mixed-use building design to correct fire-safety deficiencies. The current plan shows: (1) Group D storage separated from Group B office by a 1.5-hour wall, (2) a central exit stairwell with 1.5-hour wall rating, and (3) a Group G chemical storage room separated from adjacent Group B space by a 2-hour wall. How many of these three separations are non-compliant with Philippine codes?

options.text: Zero—all three are compliant, meeting the minimum fire-resistance requirements
One separation is non-compliant, requiring additional fireproofing measures
Two separations are non-compliant, necessitating a redesign of the fire safety plan

proposed.rationale: All three fail minimum requirements: (1) Group D requires 2-hours; (2) Multi-story exit stairs require 2-hours; (3) Group G requires 4-hours. [A]: All fail to meet the minimum standards of PD 1096 and RA 9514. [B]: More than one is incorrect. [C]: All three are deficient. [D]: Correct. 1.5-hour is too low for Storage and Stairs (2hr), and 2-hour is too low for Group G (4hr).
